The magnitude depends heavily on how far the probability moved and whether it reflects genuine leaked information versus noise; a base-case leak would knock a couple percent off, a confirmed imminent-resignation scenario could be far larger.

llm_justification.summary: This market tracks a low-probability US political tail event. A sharp jump in the implied resignation probability would most plausibly signal an acute executive-continuity/instability shock, mapping to broad US equity weakness (SPY down) and modest safe-haven gold strength (GLD up). Both mappings are low-confidence because the market is thin and noisy, the base rate is tiny, and the proxies are diffuse. Absent corroborating public reporting, treat any spike as likely noise rather than leaked signal.
key_assumptions: A meaningful, sharp increase in implied resignation probability actually occurred
The move reflects new information rather than thin-market noise or manipulation
No offsetting positive catalyst is simultaneously present
Equities and gold behave per typical risk-off/haven patterns in a political shock
failure_modes: The probability spike is thin-market noise or a manipulation flush and no asset move follows
The story was already public/priced, so equities do not react
A resignation could be read by markets as reducing uncertainty (removal of an erratic policymaker), flipping equities positive
USD strengthens as haven and gold fails to rally, breaking the second prediction
Move is below the 700bps tradable threshold, making both predictions non-actionable
